increments.title: Incoming attack telegraph state
increments.note: Validated attacks carry windup, damage, guard damage, and blockability; expiry resolves exactly one hit. No renderer or enemy-AI cue is claimed.

increments.title: Guard integrity and guard break
increments.note: Ordinary guard spends bounded guard integrity instead of health; an over-limit block breaks guard and applies the attack once.

increments.title: Perfect guard
increments.note: Guard inside the perfect window preserves health and guard integrity and grants one bounded defense counter.

increments.title: Timed dodge and perfect dodge
increments.note: Too-early dodge preserves the threat, normal evade prevents damage, and perfect dodge grants one bounded counter.

increments.title: Defense-earned Fatal Strike counter
increments.note: A valid perfect defense can reduce one eligible Fatal Strike to 35 resource; rejection does not consume the counter and successful use consumes it once.

increments.title: Forgiving perfect-defense timing preset
increments.note: Standard remains default at 0.12 s; optional forgiving preset uses 0.20 s without altering damage, resource, enemy timing, or dodge reach.

community_source.request: A way to make the satisfying but very tight Perfect Guard timing more lenient.
community_source.evidence_limit: Historical and individual community discussions, not consensus and not proof the current game retains the same timing. The implementation therefore keeps Standard unchanged and makes the wider window opt-in.

verification.repository_regression_tests: includes 8.06/7.94/794x0.01, fractional 60fps, 122-frame and 3842-frame 60Hz deadlines, 1us minimum threat, 0.120001s non-perfect guard, counter pre-expiry, and large-idle-clock rebase regressions

review_findings.finding: Repeated float subtraction could move equivalent split timing across perfect-defense and expiry boundaries.
review_findings.resolution: Reworked timing away from repeatedly subtracting float remaining time and added direct split regressions.

review_findings.finding: Per-frame integer microsecond rounding still diverged for fractional frame durations.
review_findings.resolution: Moved comparison timing to an accumulated high-precision relative clock.

review_findings.finding: A 122-frame 60Hz sequence exposed final rounding drift, and very large clocks could make newly queued deadlines unusable.
review_findings.resolution: Added explicit split-boundary normalization, idle/rebase behavior, and saturation regression coverage.

review_findings.finding: A fixed 100us tolerance expired threats early and widened the perfect window materially.
review_findings.resolution: Removed broad fixed tolerances; subsequent work replaced fixed microsecond tolerances entirely.

review_findings.finding: A fixed 2us tolerance failed longer 3842-frame splits, and a large nonsaturating absolute clock could stall short newly queued timers.
review_findings.resolution: Accumulated float-input uncertainty and cleared/rebased idle relative timing instead of carrying a large absolute clock.

review_findings.finding: Integer-microsecond quantization plus an inclusive minimum tolerance consumed a 1us threat immediately, expired a counter early, and widened a 0.120001s guard into the standard perfect window.
review_findings.resolution: Removed integer-microsecond deadline/tolerance quantization. Current code compares relative double-second timing directly with only accumulated half-ULP uncertainty from float inputs, with direct 1us threat, 0.120001s guard, counter pre-expiry, and 3842-frame regressions.
